criteria_note: Scored A-F, G, X1 and guide-specific T1-T3 (R/U/S criteria do not apply). Code was read, not executed. Prose length excludes front matter, headings, fenced code (CommonMark fence rules), display math, table rows, images and the Sources list; X's count includes about 1k chars of code that its broken fence renders as prose.

A.reason: Good arc (TL;DR -> loop -> hooks/interventions -> structured output -> approval -> controls -> retry -> state -> tracing -> when to choose) and claim headings, but line 169 ends a paragraph with an inline '```python' ('A가 연 자원을 A가 마지막에 닫게 되는 구조입니다. ```python'), so lines 171-193 render as prose with two stray H2 headings ('## excerpt: 감사 로그 훅 A와...' l171, '## A, B 순으로 등록...' l189) inside an H3 section, and the prose at 195-197 is swallowed into a code block until l212. Tangential ReAct subsection (l22-24) and orphan one-sentence paragraphs (l26 'Strands Agents는 모델 주도... SDK입니다.', l38).

B.reason: Mostly natural Korean in 입니다 register. Deductions: formulaic '결국 한 번의 호출로 메시지 네 개, 즉 두 쌍이 쌓입니다' (l79; rewrite '한 번 호출하면 메시지가 네 개, 두 쌍 쌓입니다'); translation-like 'Strands는 에이전트 루프를 직접 작성해야 할 자리에 쓰도록 설계됐습니다.' (l38); repeated hedging '서드파티 블로그는 ... 보고합니다 ... 이 블로그에 따르면 ... 같은 블로그는 ... 설명합니다' (l1081, l1093); English cells in a Korean table ('Before the agent loop starts', l245-249).

C.reason: Running example ties sections, but hooks code uses lookup_customer before it is defined and the post admits it later ('앞선 훅 예제들이 정의 없이 써 온 lookup_customer를 여기서 정의합니다', l421); ReAct paragraph (l24) and the l26 sentence read as stitched fragments; '하네스도 함께 검토할 만합니다' (l1103) relies on a concept never introduced; l1093 says there are 'two gaps to fill' but the second only restates that telemetry goes to span events without saying what breaks.

D.reason: Hard parts get worked examples at the right time: message counting (l79), hook order A/B (l169), RateLimiter/Validator trace (l264), token overshoot 6,000+5,000 (l679), fail-open vs fail-closed (l335-358). Padding: the ReAct experiment numbers (l24) are not needed by a Strands user; the window_size worked example (l139) teaches a wrong mental model.

E.reason: Useful tables (stop reasons l99, intervention methods/actions l243-258, checkpoints l687, retry params l826, state layers l939, limits l1123) and an ASCII loop diagram. Missing a hook-event list although Hooks is a primary source; Datadog screenshot (l1087) is a remote hot-linked marketing image; English source cells left untranslated in a Korean table (l245-249).

F.reason: One factual error with a downstream wrong example: 'SlidingWindowConversationManager는 최근 N개의 메시지 쌍을 유지' and 'window_size=10, # 유지할 최대 메시지 쌍 수' (l126, l133) vs docs 'Maximum number of messages to keep'; hence 'window_size=10일 때 대략 최근 다섯 건의 티켓' (l139) is wrong (about 2.5 tickets). Other 30 checked claims supported; third-party claims are attributed.

G.reason: No math, so no use_math is correct; description 120 chars (at the lower bound), opens with the product name. The broken fence at l169 produces stray headings and swaps code/prose rendering (blog lint would flag body H2 inside H3 and broken code); remote image with query string (l1087); stray leading space at l832.

X1.reason: Controlled tag Agentic-AI plus product and feature tags (Strands-Agents-SDK, Agent-Loop, Structured-Output); 'Human-in-the-Loop-Approval' and 'OpenTelemetry-Tracing' are long, low-reuse spellings.

T1.reason: Concrete Python code for one ticket-triage app with real arguments (limits, cancel_signal, structured_output_model, HumanInTheLoop, SnapshotSessionManager). But the assembled service handler handle_ticket uses HumanInTheLoop(ask='stdio') inside a per-request server function (l794), which would block on terminal input in a service; several snippets are excerpts relying on later definitions (l171, l219, l267); the broken fence at l169 makes one example unreadable as code.

T2.reason: Agent loop page is well covered; Hooks page only partly (ordering, tool interception, resume, retry hooks) while the event catalogue, cancel_tool/limit-tool-count, exception propagation and multi-agent hooks are absent. Adds sessions, HITL, Cedar and telemetry from other official pages (supported) plus a ReAct experiment summary (l24) that is padding.

T3.reason: Explains why mechanisms are designed as they are (schema-as-tool, typed interventions vs mutating hooks, cooperative cancellation, fail-open vs fail-closed) and how the agent fits a system (per-request agents, session storage trust boundary and lack of locks, OTLP backends, telemetry PII). Includes non-official sources (Datadog, New Relic) clearly framed as reports.
